overview: The Panama City Community Redevelopment Agency was created in 1983. The City Commission sits as its board, and it currently runs four tax-increment districts: Downtown (1984), St. Andrews (1989, expanded 2025), Downtown North/Glenwood (1993, expanded several times) and Millville (2004). City and Bay County tax increment provided about $1.6M a year in the early 2010s, roughly $1.3M in FY2021 after Hurricane Michael, and about $3.0-3.6M by FY2024-25. The money pays for 50/50 business and residential improvement grants, park and waterfront projects (Millville Waterfront Park, the Bayview Boardwalk, McKenzie Park), streetscape and beautification work, community policing, maintenance MOUs, a 2024 TIF rebate incentive program for private developers, and the 2025 Glenwood Town Center land deal. All districts are scheduled to sunset in 2044.

districts.name: Downtown
districts.boundary_description: Historic downtown core around Harrison Ave. Massalina Bayou forms the east edge and St. Andrews Bay the southwest edge, and the north edge is shared with Downtown North (around 11th/12th St). Administered historically with the Downtown Improvement Board.

districts.name: St. Andrews
districts.boundary_description: Historic St. Andrews waterfront and the Beck Ave corridor. It runs south to St. Andrews Bay and north along both sides of W. US 98 (15th St). The 2025 expansion (about 672 acres, per WJHG) extended the district along 15th St/US 98 west to the Hathaway Bridge and east to Lisenby Ave. Bay County keeps 26% of the increment from the expansion area. The polygon shows the original core only.

districts.name: Downtown North (Glenwood)
districts.boundary_description: North of downtown from about 12th St north to US 231, between McKenzie Ave and Mercedes Ave. Includes the Greater Glenwood neighborhood, the MLK Blvd (SR 77) corridor and Bay Medical. Later expansions added the area bounded by W. 12th St, US 231 and McKenzie Ave, the former Panama City Mall site north of US 231 (2021), and an area east of Mercedes Ave between E. 13th St and US 231 (2021). The city's documents give slightly different expansion years.

districts.name: Millville
districts.boundary_description: Bounded by 7th St North (north), Everitt Ave (east), Cherry St (south) and Watson Bayou (west), plus a small area west of Watson Bayou around Cove Point Drive. Includes the Business US 98 (E. 3rd St/E. 5th St) corridor and Millville (Watson Bayou) Waterfront Park.

controversies.summary: Michael Johnson, the city's former community development director, was charged in 2021 with embezzling from the Friends of After School Assistance Program. In March 2023 he pleaded no contest to grand theft, money laundering and 19 counts of official misconduct and was sentenced to 8 years. The CRA's FY2022 audit says a former key employee was convicted of misappropriating $83,390 from the Downtown North CRA, and it restated the prior year's financial statements for fraud-related disallowed costs.

Warren Averett's forensic audit (reported June 2023) concluded Johnson acted alone. It found roughly $89,000 taken from the CRA and about $1 million from Friends of ASAP, and found that CRA money was used to renovate four of his personal rental properties, which the city seized to sell.

Audited statements for several years show internal inconsistencies. The tax increment figure in Note 1 does not match the revenue statements in FY2021-FY2024, and FY2023 expenditures exceeded appropriations by $935,842.

The 447 Harrison Ave breezeway was acquired through a land swap with investor George Kingston's company and renovated with CRA funds. Its plans changed several times, budgets ranged from $81,000 to $700,000 across documents, and in 2025 officials considered selling it to a developer.

During the 2025 St. Andrews expansion, some residents questioned whether inclusion in the CRA would benefit their properties. Bay County approved the expansion only after negotiating to keep 26% of the increment from the new area.

The CRA discontinued its business grant programs in September 2023 and later reopened them only for hardship cases. The board approved a multi-year, $4.5M in-house road repair plan on a 3-2 vote, with Josh Street and Robbie Hughes dissenting.

data_gaps: No district-level TIF or budget figures were found for FY2019-FY2020 (the FY2019 and FY2020 audits on flauditor.gov were unreadable or failed to load). Those annual reports and audits likely sit in the panamacity.gov Document Center or Archive Center, or can be had by records request.

Grant recipient names are mostly missing before FY2024. Annual reports give aggregate 50/50 grant totals. Grant agreements and check registers would require a public records request to the CRA (cras@panamacity.gov).
Price and seller for the April 2017 purchase of 37 lots and 35 homes on 6.5 acres in Downtown North. Check Bay County property appraiser and clerk deed records.

The CRA's share of the roughly $7M Harrison Ave streetscape (2021-2025). Public sources cite a $5.7M state agreement and $5.6M CDBG-DR Project HEART but no CRA amount. Check CRA board agendas for 2021-2025.
Final terms and sale price of the 2025 Sankofa Group Glenwood Town Center agreement (the proposal offered $667,099.62). The development agreement is in the July 2025 CRA agenda packet.

Contract values for consultants (GAI Consultants plan update, AECOM marina master plan, Retail Strategies actuals) and for construction contractors (Mainline Construction, CBC Construction, VBA/Florida Architects).

Downtown Marina/Bay County Marina and St. Andrews Marina rebuilds appear to be funded mainly by the city, FEMA and grants. No CRA payment amounts were found. The 2026 St. Andrews Marina cost-plus contract amount was not reported.

Hurricane Michael recovery: CDBG-DR Hometown Revitalization facade grants ($20.1M across CRA corridors) are city/state funds, not CRA TIF, so they are excluded from payments. CRA-specific post-storm spending in FY2019-2020 is undocumented online.

Precise district boundary shapefiles are not available. Polygons are rough sketches from the street boundaries described in the 2025 plan and should be replaced with city GIS data (Panama City GIS or a Bay County request).

No Glenwood, Bayou George/Lake Caroline or Cove/East CRA districts exist as separate districts. Glenwood is part of Downtown North. The Cove area got a $12.949M city contract, but no CRA district covers it.

FY2027 CRA budget (added 2026-10-21): Resolution CRA20260901.1 gives Millville $1,228,009, but the attached proposed budget table totals $1,288,009 ($1,186,625 TIF plus $101,384 reserves). The FY2027 rows use the table. FY2027 totals include $5.15M of planned debt proceeds for St. Andrews and Downtown. No FY2025 Auditor General filing for the Panama City CRA was found on flauditor.gov.
